title.official: Joint Statement EU-US Trade and Technology Council of 4-5 April 2024 in Leuven, Belgium

relevance.reason: The AI section of the sixth U.S.–EU Trade and Technology Council joint statement records a political commitment by the European AI Office and the U.S. AI Safety Institute to establish a Dialogue for scientific information exchange on benchmarks, potential risks and future technological trends. It is not a standalone US–EU AI-safety MOU, administrative arrangement or treaty; no separate terms of reference or binding text was located. The record catalogues the joint statement because it is the primary source of the commitment.
ai_provisions: The parties reaffirm a risk-based approach to AI and coordination in the G7, OECD, G20, Council of Europe and UN processes.
Leaders from the European AI Office and the U.S. AI Safety Institute briefed one another on their approaches and mandates.
The two institutions 'committed to establishing a Dialogue' to deepen collaboration and foster scientific information exchange on benchmarks, potential risks and future technological trends.
The cooperation is linked to the Joint Roadmap on Evaluation and Measurement Tools for Trustworthy AI and Risk Management and to interoperable international standards.
The parties encourage advanced AI developers to apply the Hiroshima Process International Code of Conduct.
relevance.excluded_scope: The joint statement is broad — trade, technology, standards, economic security and human rights. Only the AI-related commitments are catalogued. There is no standalone AI-safety agreement, MOU, administrative arrangement, binding obligation, ratification or dispute settlement.

dates.notes: Sixth ministerial meeting of the U.S.–EU Trade and Technology Council, Leuven, 4–5 April 2024; the joint statement was published on 5 April 2024. The first technical Dialogue under the commitment was held on 11 July 2024.

status_note: Political joint statement, not a treaty. The AI-safety commitment is the establishment of a Dialogue between the European AI Office and the U.S. AI Safety Institute. No standalone US–EU AI-safety MOU, administrative arrangement or terms of reference was located. The separate U.S.–EU Administrative Arrangement on AI and computing is a research-cooperation instrument, not an AI-safety agreement. The joint statement creates no binding obligations, ratification, depositary or dispute settlement.

languages.note: English versions published by the European Commission and the U.S. Trade Representative were read. Other language versions were not checked; there is no authentic-language clause because the instrument is not a treaty.
